newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end marginally higher in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end marginally higher in light trade.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed marginally higher on Monday helped by buying of a limited number of issues, backed partly by solid corporate earnings reports. Market participants were still cautious over the currency market and Wall Street stocks, brokers said.
A stream of annual earnings results reported by Japanese trust banks and long-term credit banks on Monday had been largely factored in by the market and had little impact on the key index, they said.
The 225-share Nikkei average gained 34.50 points or 0.17 percent to finish the session at 20,043.50.
The key index hovered within a range of 19,989.10 to 20,154.52.
Its June futures were up 120 points at 20,150.
"People were seeking fresh factors to trade on, as the Nikkei 225 was trapped in a boxed range," said Michio Sugita, head of stock trading at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Turnover was light, with 269 million shares changing hands on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange on Monday, down from 368 million shares on Friday.
Declining issues slightly outnumbered advancers 552 to 505, while 185 issues were unchanged.
In other indices, the broader TOPIX index edged up 4.72 points or 0.32 percent to end at 1,494.61. The Nikkei 300 average was up 1.19 point or 0.41 percent at 289.26.
Caution over the currency market, where participants see possible further fluctuations, limited trading in stocks.

"Since currencies' direction is not clear, the market turned its attention to a limited number of issues with a factor to buy, such as IC (integrated circuit) cards," said Kaoru Ichikawa, a senior trader at Kokusai Securities Co Ltd.
But some analysts expected export-driven shares, which were dented by the yen's rally recently, to resume rising.

"A rally in blue-chip exporters paused, but high-tech issues in particular are expected to gain more ground in the long term, as the trend of the weaker yen has not changed," said Keiko Kondo, a strategist at Merrill Lynch Japan Inc.
Shares in Shinko Electric Co Ltd surged on hopes that the IC phone card business will benefit the firm's profits.

Shares of the medium-sized electrical machinery maker jumped 80 yen or 20.67 percent to close at 467, a high for this calendar year, making the firm the second-biggest percentage gainer on the first section.
Shinko was also the third most heavily traded issue at 3.764 million shares.

Telecommunications equipment maker Tamura Electric Works Ltd also rose on hopes of IC phone card business, adding 90 yen to close at 895, making it the fifth biggest percentage gainer on the first section. The shares briefly hit a high for this calendar year of 900 yen.
Shares in Sumitomo Trust & Banking Co Ltd and Toyo Trust & Banking Co Ltd fell on a newspaper report that said they were planning to issue convertible bonds overseas.
Sumitomo Trust was down 20 yen at 1,070.
Toyo Trust lost seven yen to end at 824.
Sumitomo Trust later said it would issue yen-denominated subordinated convertible bonds worth up to 110 billion yen through its wholly owned overseas unit STB Cayman Capital Ltd.

Toyo Trust also said in late afternoon that it would issue Euroyen subordinated bonds of 50 billion yen through its overseas unit and that it would also issue Euroyen convertibles worth 50 billion yen.
Shares of Nippon Credit Bank Ltd, whose weak financial health hurt the market early this year, ended almost flat, down two yen at 247, after release of its earnings.
The bank said its parent current losses were 350.16 billion yen for 1996/97 fiscal year, against its parent current losses of 131.16 billion yen the year before.

By sector, gainers were led by automobiles, brokerages, trading houses, railway/bus and precision instruments. The major losers were sea transport, mining, real estate, communications and miscellaneous manufacturing.
The second section index was up 1.70 points at 1,760.47, with 9.7 million shares traded. The over-the-counter (OTC) index was down 1.01 points at 1,179.95.
-- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027
